unit: Unit III — Cell: Structure and Function
title: Protein Structural Hierarchy: 1°, 2°, 3°, & 4° Organization
topic: Alpha-Helices, Beta-Sheets, Disulfide Bridges, & Hemoglobin Quaternary Tetramer
topics: Four Levels of Protein Structural Organization
Primary Structure ($1^\circ$: Covalent Peptide Backbone, N- to C-Terminus)
Secondary Structure ($2^\circ$: Backbone H-Bonds, 3.6 Residues/Turn $\alpha$-Helix, $\beta$-Pleated Sheets)
Tertiary Structure ($3^\circ$: 3D Globular Conformation, Hydrophobic Interactions, Disulfide $-S-S-$ Bonds)
Biological Activity Requirement of Tertiary Structure
Quaternary Structure ($4^\circ$: Multisubunit Oligomers, Adult Hemoglobin $\alpha_2\beta_2$ Tetramer)
quickSummary: Protein architecture comprises 4 levels: 1) Primary (linear peptide sequence from N- to C-terminus), 2) Secondary (local folding stabilized strictly by backbone H-bonds: right-handed α-helix with 3.6 residues/turn and β-pleated sheets), 3) Tertiary (compact 3D globular architecture stabilized by hydrophobic packing, disulfide covalent crosslinks, ionic salt bridges; required for biological enzyme activity), and 4) Quaternary (spatial assembly of multiple subunits, e.g., adult hemoglobin HbA tetramer α2β2).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Detailed Levels of Protein Organization
conceptBreakdown.title: Detailed Levels of Protein Organization
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Primary Structure ($1^\circ$)**: The specific linear sequence of amino acids linked covalently by peptide bonds from the N-terminal amino acid to the C-terminal amino acid.
2. **Secondary Structure ($2^\circ$)**: Local spatial conformation of the polypeptide backbone stabilized **exclusively by Hydrogen Bonds** between backbone carbonyl oxygens ($\text{C}=\text{O}$) and amide nitrogens ($\text{N}-\text{H}$):
   - **$\alpha$-Helix**: Right-handed rod-like coil containing **3.6 amino acid residues per turn** with a pitch of $0.54\text{ nm}$ ($5.4\ \text{\AA}$). Hydrogen bonds form between residue $i$ and residue $i+4$.
   - **$\beta$-Pleated Sheets**: Extended polypeptide strands running parallel or anti-parallel, linked by inter-strand hydrogen bonds.
3. **Tertiary Structure ($3^\circ$)**: Bending, twisting, and folding of the polypeptide chain into a compact **3D globular conformation**. Stabilized by:
   - **Hydrophobic interactions** (non-polar side chains buried internally).
   - **Disulfide bonds** (covalent $-\text{S}-\text{S}-$ links between Cysteines).
   - **Ionic / Salt bridges** (between $-\text{COO}^-$ and $-\text{NH}_3^+$ side chains).
   - **Hydrogen bonds & van der Waals forces**.
   - *Tertiary structure is strictly mandatory for biological enzymatic and immunological activity*.
4. **Quaternary Structure ($4^\circ$)**: The 3D spatial assembly of two or more individual polypeptide chains (protomers/subunits) into a single functional oligomer (*e.g., Adult Hemoglobin $\text{HbA}$ is a tetramer of $2\alpha$ and $2\beta$ chains: $\alpha_2\beta_2$*).
